items.title: Differential Privacy for Euclidean Jordan Algebra with Applications to Private Symmetric Cone Programming
items.one_liner: A new generic Gaussian mechanism for Euclidean Jordan algebras solves a long-standing open question in differentially private semidefinite programming.

items.title: SnapAudit: Active Auditing of Differentially Private In-Context Learning via Snapshot-Based Simulation
items.one_liner: SnapAudit uses snapshot-based simulation to efficiently audit differentially private in-context learning, uncovering hidden privacy leakage flaws.
items.summary: Verifying differential privacy (DP) guarantees in in-context learning (ICL) pipelines through repeated end-to-end membership-inference attacks is computationally expensive and unstable. To solve this, researchers introduce SnapAudit, an active auditing framework that separates the pipeline into a deterministic clean-inference stage and a stochastic DP-noise stage, using snapshot simulation to reduce costs. By avoiding repeated end-to-end trials, SnapAudit reduces total wall-clock auditing time by 4.3 to 5.5 times across multiple pipelines and privacy budgets. Furthermore, the tool uncovered fundamental flaws in existing DP-ICl designs, including underestimated leakage at large privacy budgets and incorrect sensitivity analysis in specific embedding-aggregation mechanisms.

items.bottom_line: SnapAudit cuts DP-ICL auditing time by up to 5.5x while uncovering critical sensitivity and noise calibration flaws in existing privacy mechanisms.

items.title: Nash Incentive-compatible Online Mechanism Learning via Weakly Differentially Private Online Learning
items.one_liner: A novel online learning mechanism combines weak differential privacy with commitment rules to ensure multi-round incentive compatibility.
items.summary: This paper addresses multi-round mechanism design problems involving a sequence of strategic agents without prior knowledge of their type distributions. A naive online learning approach can fail to be incentive-compatible against non-myopic buyers who participate across multiple rounds. To fix this, the authors propose a method that randomly chooses between the recommendations of a weakly differentially private online learning algorithm and a commitment mechanism penalizing non-truthful behavior. This scheme achieves strategic incentive compatibility and provides strong regret bounds that scale gracefully with the size of the mechanism class.
items.bottom_line: Combining weak differential privacy with commitment penalties enables multi-round incentive compatibility and bounded regret for general mechanism design.

items.title: From Attack Surface to Defense Architecture: Compositional Security for Agentic Coding Harnesses
items.one_liner: ActiveSecHarness introduces a neurosymbolic reference monitor architecture to secure AI coding agent harnesses against Living-off-the-Land attacks.
items.summary: AI coding harnesses often expose models directly to shells and filesystems, allowing prompt injections in retrieved content to abuse dual-use binaries like bash and curl. To secure these environments, researchers propose ActiveSecHarness, a neurosymbolic reference monitor that separates intelligence from authority. The architecture combines HMAC capability tokens across four trust rings, a 2D product taint lattice, workspace provenance ledgers, and deterministic OS/tool guards. Benchmarks demonstrate that the neurosymbolic reference monitor achieves high attack blocking with zero false positives while executing significantly faster than LLM-as-a-judge solutions.
items.bottom_line: ActiveSecHarness secures AI coding harnesses using a neurosymbolic architecture with HMAC capability tokens and a 2D product taint lattice.

items.title: Agent Architecture Cost-Success Trade-offs: A Controlled Evaluation across Enterprise-Style SOPs
items.one_liner: A controlled evaluation of LLM agent architectures reveals that single agents with high-quality skills outperform complex multi-agent frameworks at a fraction of the cost.
items.summary: A controlled evaluation across 13 enterprise standard operating procedures (SOPs) examined the cost-success trade-offs of four LLM agent architectures: function-calling single agents, skill-augmented agents, centralized multi-agent orchestration, and triage swarms. The study found no universal best architecture, with added coordination structures increasing token consumption by 1.4 to 4.7 times and latency by 2.6 to 5.8 times without yielding statistically significant success gains in most scenarios. Implementation quality and high-quality skill definitions proved far more impactful than architectural complexity, establishing the single agent as the efficient default for enterprise workflows.
items.bottom_line: Complex multi-agent architectures incur massive token and latency penalties without reliable success gains, making single agents with good skills the efficient enterprise default.

items.title: BuySideFlow: A Point-in-Time Benchmark for LLM Agents in Investment Research
items.one_liner: BuySideFlow benchmark evaluates LLM investment research agents, exposing widespread point-in-time validity failures.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced BuySideFlow, a benchmark featuring 408 practitioner-derived Chinese-language financial tasks across equities, funds, fixed income, and macroeconomics. Designed to evaluate LLM agents in investment research, the benchmark measures point-in-time (PIT) validity, ensuring agents correctly handle historical record versions and disclosure cutoffs. Evaluating nine agent configurations, result accuracy ranged from 16.2% to 36.8%, and expert audits revealed that 50.8% of runs passing basic result checks contained temporal validation errors, proving that output agreement alone does not guarantee temporal correctness.

items.bottom_line: Over half of LLM agent workflows that pass financial result checks suffer from point-in-time temporal validity violations, according to the BuySideFlow benchmark.

items.one_liner: Attackers are actively compromising MSPs by abusing ScreenConnect's legitimate remote management features to deploy unauthorized access tools.
items.summary: An active malware campaign is targeting managed service providers (MSPs) by compromising cloud-hosted ScreenConnect instances. Attackers are abusing legitimate ScreenConnect functionality, such as the Run Command feature, to deploy rogue remote-access clients on customer endpoints.
